sanskrit: nigṛhya ca gadāḥ ke cit pārśvasthair bhṛśadāruṇaiḥ rathāśvasādibhis tatra saṃbhinnā nyapatan bhuvi
english: Some, gripping their maces, were broken apart there by the cruel warriors who stood at their flanks—charioteers, horsemen, and the rest—and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: sarathaṃ sādinaṃ tatra apare tu mahāgajāḥ bhūmāv amṛdnan vegena savarmāṇaṃ patākinam
english: Other great elephants there crushed to the earth with their rush a rider together with his chariot, armored and bearing his banner.

sanskrit: rathaṃ nāgāḥ samāsādya dhuri gṛhya ca māriṣa vyākṣipan sahasā tatra ghorarūpe mahāmṛdhe
english: The elephants, falling upon a chariot and seizing it by the yoke-pole, O sir, suddenly flung it about there in that ghastly, mighty battle.

sanskrit: nārācair nihataś cāpi nipapāta mahāgajaḥ parvatasyeva śikharaṃ vajrabhagnaṃ mahītale
english: And a great elephant, struck down by iron shafts, fell to the ground like the peak of a mountain shattered by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: yodhā yodhān samāsādya muṣṭibhir vyahanan yudhi keśeṣv anyonyam ākṣipya cicchidur bibhiduḥ saha
english: Warriors, closing with warriors, struck one another with their fists in the fight, and seizing each other by the hair, they cut and pierced one another together.

sanskrit: udyamya ca bhujāv anyo nikṣipya ca mahītale padā coraḥ samākramya sphurato vyahanac chiraḥ
english: And another, raising his arms and casting his foe upon the ground, set his foot upon the breast of the still-quivering man and struck off his head.

sanskrit: mṛtam anyo mahārāja padbhyāṃ tāḍitavāṃs tadā jīvataś ca tathaivānyaḥ śastraṃ kāye nyamajjayat
english: Another, O great king, trampled a dead man with his feet, while yet another plunged his weapon into the body of one still living.

sanskrit: muṣṭiyuddhaṃ mahac cāsīd yodhānāṃ tatra bhārata tathā keśagrahaś cogro bāhuyuddhaṃ ca kevalam
english: A great combat of fists arose among the warriors there, O Bhārata, and fierce seizing of hair, and bare wrestling with the arms alone.

sanskrit: samāsaktasya cānyena avijñātas tathāparaḥ jahāra samare prāṇān nānāśastrair anekadhā
english: While one was locked in struggle with another, a third, unnoticed, took his life in the battle with manifold weapons in many ways.

sanskrit: saṃsakteṣu ca yodheṣu vartamāne ca saṃkule kabandhāny utthitāni sma śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: As the warriors clashed and the tumult raged on, headless trunks rose up by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: lohitaiḥ sicyamānāni śastrāṇi kavacāni ca mahāraṅgānuraktāni vastrāṇīva cakāśire
english: Drenched in blood, the weapons and the coats of mail gleamed like garments dyed in a deep crimson hue.

sanskrit: evam etan mahāyuddhaṃ dāruṇaṃ bhṛśasaṃkulam unmattaraṅgapratimaṃ śabdenāpūrayaj jagat
english: Thus that great battle, dreadful and utterly confused, like a frenzied dancing-stage, filled the whole world with its uproar.

sanskrit: naiva sve na pare rājan vijñāyante śarāturāḥ yoddhavyam iti yudhyante rājāno jayagṛddhinaḥ
english: Neither friend nor foe could be told apart, O king, by the men tormented with arrows; the kings, greedy for victory, fought only because there was fighting to be done.

sanskrit: svān sve jaghnur mahārāja parāṃś caiva samāgatān ubhayoḥ senayor vīrair vyākulaṃ samapadyata
english: Their own men slew their own, O great king, and the foes they met as well; through the heroes of both armies all became confusion.

sanskrit: rathair bhagnair mahārāja vāraṇaiś ca nipātitaiḥ hayaiś ca patitais tatra naraiś ca vinipātitaiḥ
english: With chariots broken, O great king, and elephants brought down, with horses fallen there and men struck to the ground,

sanskrit: agamyarūpā pṛthivī māṃsaśoṇitakardamā kṣaṇenāsīn mahārāja kṣatajaughapravartinī
english: the earth became impassable, a mire of flesh and blood, and in a moment, O great king, it flowed with streams of gore.

sanskrit: pāñcālān avadhīt karṇas trigartāṃś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ bhīmasenaḥ kurūn rājan hastyanīkaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Karṇa slew the Pāñcālas, and Dhanaṃjaya the Trigartas; Bhīmasena, O king, slew the Kurus and their whole host of elephants.

sanskrit: evam eṣa kṣayo vṛttaḥ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ aparāhṇe mahārāja kāṅkṣantyor vipulaṃ jayam
english: Thus this destruction came to pass between the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas in the afternoon, O great king, as both longed for an ample victory.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca atitīvrāṇi duḥkhāni duḥsahāni bahūni ca tavāhaṃ saṃjayāśrauṣaṃ putrāṇāṃ mama saṃkṣayam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Most piercing sorrows, hard to bear and many, have I heard from you, Saṃjaya—the destruction of my sons.

sanskrit: tathā tu me kathayase yathā yuddhaṃ tu vartate na santi sūta kauravyā iti me naiṣṭhikī matiḥ
english: From the way you recount to me how the battle proceeds, my settled conviction, O bard, is this: the Kauravas are no more.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu virathaḥ kṛtas tatra mahāraṇe dharmaputraḥ kathaṃ cakre tasmin vā nṛpatiḥ katham
english: When Duryodhana was made chariotless there in that great battle, what did the son of Dharma do, and how did the king fare in that contest?

sanskrit: aparāhṇe kathaṃ yuddham abhaval lomaharṣaṇam tan mamācakṣva tattvena kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: How did the hair-raising battle unfold in the afternoon? Tell me that truly, Saṃjaya, for you are skilled in the telling.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃsakteṣu ca sainyeṣu yudhyamāneṣu bhāgaśaḥ ratham anyaṃ samāsthāya putras tava viśāṃ pate
english: Saṃjaya said: As the armies clashed and fought, division against division, your son, O lord of peoples, mounted another chariot.

sanskrit: krodhena mahatāviṣṭaḥ saviṣo bhujago yathā duryodhanas tu dṛṣṭvā vai dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram uvāca sūta tvaritaṃ yāhi yāhīti bhārata
english: Seized with great wrath, like a venomous serpent, Duryodhana, beholding the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira, said to his driver: "Go, O charioteer, go swiftly!" O Bhārata.

sanskrit: atra māṃ prāpaya kṣipraṃ sārathe yatra pāṇḍavaḥ dhriyamāṇena chatreṇa rājā rājati daṃśitaḥ
english: "Bring me quickly, O charioteer, to where the Pāṇḍava is—where the king, armored, shines beneath his held-aloft parasol."

sanskrit: sa sūtaś codito rājñā rājñaḥ syandanam uttamam yudhiṣṭhirasyābhimukhaṃ preṣayām āsa saṃyuge
english: That charioteer, urged on by the king, sent the king's splendid chariot straight toward Yudhiṣṭhira in the fray.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kruddhaḥ pramatta iva sadgavaḥ sārathiṃ codayām āsa yāhi yatra suyodhanaḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, enraged like a noble bull run wild, urged on his charioteer: "Go to where Suyodhana is!"

sanskrit: tau samājagmatur vīrau bhrātarau rathasattamau sametya ca mahāvīryau saṃnaddhau yuddhadurmadau tatakṣatur maheṣvāsau śarair anyonyam āhave
english: The two heroes met, those brothers, the foremost of charioteers; and meeting, the two of mighty valor, mailed and battle-frenzied, those great archers, hewed at one another with their arrows in the combat.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā dharmaśīlasya māriṣa śilāśitena bhallena dhanuś ciccheda saṃyuge taṃ nāmṛṣyata saṃkruddho vyavasāyaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then king Duryodhana, O sir, with a stone-whetted broad-headed shaft severed the bow of the righteous-natured one in the fight; but Yudhiṣṭhira, enraged, would not brook that bold stroke.

sanskrit: apavidhya dhanuś chinnaṃ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ anyat kārmukam ādāya dharmaputraś camūmukhe
english: Casting aside the severed bow, his eyes red with rage, the son of Dharma took up another bow at the head of the host,

sanskrit: duryodhanasya ciccheda dhvajaṃ kārmukam eva ca athānyad dhanur ādāya pratyavidhyata pāṇḍavam
english: and cut off Duryodhana's banner and his bow as well; then Duryodhana, taking up another bow, pierced the Pāṇḍava in return.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ susaṃrabdhau śaravarṣāṇy amuñcatām siṃhāv iva susaṃkruddhau parasparajigīṣayā
english: The two, deeply roused against each other, loosed showers of arrows, like two lions wholly enraged, each longing to conquer the other.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ jaghnatuś caiva nardamānau vṛṣāv iva anyonyaṃ prekṣamāṇau ca ceratus tau mahārathau
english: They smote one another, bellowing like bulls, and those two great car-warriors ranged about, eyeing each other.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair anyonyaṃ sukṛtavraṇau virejatur mahārāja puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Then, well wounded by shafts loosed from bows drawn to their full length, the two shone, O great king, like a pair of kiṃśuka trees in blossom.

sanskrit: tato rājan pratibhayān siṃhanādān muhur muhuḥ talayoś ca tathā śabdān dhanuṣoś ca mahāhave
english: Then, O king, in that great battle, the terrifying lion-roars again and again, and the clapping of palms, and the twang of bows,

sanskrit: śaṅkhaśabdaravāṃś caiva cakratus tau rathottamau anyonyaṃ ca mahārāja pīḍayāṃ cakratur bhṛśam
english: and the blaring of conches—all these those two foremost car-warriors made, and they pressed one another hard, O great king.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā tava putraṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghānorasi kruddho vajravego durāsadaḥ
english: Then king Yudhiṣṭhira, enraged, with the speed of the thunderbolt and hard to withstand, struck your son in the breast with three arrows.

sanskrit: prativivyādha taṃ tūrṇaṃ tava putro mahīpatim pañcabhir niśitair bāṇair hemapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Your son swiftly pierced that lord of earth in return with five sharp, gold-feathered, stone-whetted arrows.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā śaktiṃ cikṣepa bhārata sarvapāraśavīṃ tīkṣṇāṃ maholkāpratimāṃ tadā
english: Then king Duryodhana hurled a lance, O Bhārata—all of steel, keen, and like a great blazing meteor.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā dharmarājaḥ śilāśitaiḥ tribhiś ciccheda sahasā taṃ ca vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: As it sped down upon him, the Dharma-king at once cut it through with three stone-whetted shafts, and pierced him with seven.

sanskrit: nipapāta tataḥ sātha hemadaṇḍā mahāghanā nipatantī maholkeva vyarājac chikhisaṃnibhā
english: Then that lance with its golden shaft, massive and heavy, fell down, and as it fell it shone like a great meteor, resembling fire itself.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā putras tava viśāṃ pate navabhir niśitair bhallair nijaghāna yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Seeing his lance struck down, your son, O lord of peoples, smote Yudhiṣṭhira with nine sharp broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatām agraṇīḥ śatrutāpanaḥ duryodhanaṃ samuddiśya bāṇaṃ jagrāha satvaraḥ
english: Sorely wounded, that foremost of the mighty, the scorcher of foes, quickly took up an arrow, aiming at Duryodhana,

sanskrit: samādhatta ca taṃ bāṇaṃ dhanuṣy ugraṃ mahābalaḥ cikṣepa ca tato rājā rājñaḥ kruddhaḥ parākramī
english: and that mighty one fitted the fierce arrow to his bow; then the king, valorous and enraged, loosed it at the king.

sanskrit: sa tu bāṇaḥ samāsādya tava putraṃ mahāratham vyamohayata rājānaṃ dharaṇīṃ ca jagāma ha
english: That arrow, reaching your son, the great car-warrior, stunned the king into a swoon, and then passed on into the earth.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ kruddho gadām udyamya vegitaḥ vidhitsuḥ kalahasyāntam abhidudrāva pāṇḍavam
english: Then Duryodhana, enraged, raising his mace and rushing on with speed, eager to make an end of the quarrel, charged at the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tam ālakṣyodyatagadaṃ daṇḍahastam ivāntakam dharmarājo mahāśaktiṃ prāhiṇot tava sūnave dīpyamānāṃ mahāvegāṃ maholkāṃ jvalitām iva
english: Marking him with mace upraised, like Death with rod in hand, the Dharma-king hurled at your son a great lance, blazing, of mighty speed, like a flaming meteor.

sanskrit: rathasthaḥ sa tayā viddho varma bhittvā mahāhave bhṛśaṃ saṃvignahṛdayaḥ papāta ca mumoha ca
english: Standing in his chariot, pierced by it as it broke through his armor in that great battle, his heart utterly shaken, he both fell and swooned.

sanskrit: tatas tvaritam āgatya kṛtavarmā tavātmajam pratyapadyata rājānaṃ magnaṃ vai vyasanārṇave
english: Then Kṛtavarman, coming swiftly, came to the aid of your son, the king, who was sunk indeed in an ocean of distress.

sanskrit: bhīmo 'pi mahatīṃ gṛhya gadāṃ hemapariṣkṛtām abhidudrāva vegena kṛtavarmāṇam āhave evaṃ tad abhavad yuddhaṃ tvadīyānāṃ paraiḥ saha
english: Bhīma too, seizing his great gold-adorned mace, rushed with speed upon Kṛtavarman in the battle. Thus did that fight of your men with the foe come to pass.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ karṇaṃ puraskṛtya tvadīyā yuddhadurmadāḥ punar āvṛtya saṃgrāmaṃ cakrur devāsuropamam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, with Karṇa at their head, your men, frenzied for battle, turned back once more and waged a combat like that of gods and demons.

sanskrit: dviradarathanarāśvaśaṅkhaśabdaiḥ; parihṛṣitā vividhaiś ca śastrapātaiḥ dviradarathapadātisārthavāhāḥ; paripatitābhimukhāḥ prajahrire te
english: Thrilled by the sounds of elephants, chariots, men, horses, and conches, and by the manifold falling of weapons, the throngs of elephants, chariots, and foot-soldiers, rushing face to face, fell upon one another and struck.

sanskrit: śaraparaśuvarāsipaṭṭiśair; iṣubhir anekavidhaiś ca sāditāḥ dviradarathahayā mahāhave; varapuruṣaiḥ puruṣāś ca vāhanaiḥ
english: By arrows, axes, fine swords, and pikes, and by shafts of many kinds, the elephants, chariots, and horses were laid low in that great battle by the best of men, and men were laid low by the war-beasts.

sanskrit: kamaladinakarendusaṃnibhaiḥ; sitadaśanaiḥ sumukhākṣināsikaiḥ ruciramukuṭakuṇḍalair mahī; puruṣaśirobhir avastṛtā babhau
english: With the heads of men—like lotuses, like the sun, like the moon, with white teeth and fair faces, eyes, and noses, and with gleaming diadems and earrings—the earth lay strewn and shone.

sanskrit: parighamusalaśaktitomarair; nakharabhuśuṇḍigadāśatair drutāḥ dviradanarahayāḥ sahasraśo; rudhiranadīpravahās tadābhavan
english: Smitten by iron clubs, pestles, lances, and javelins, by claw-knives, slings, and hundreds of maces, the elephants, men, and horses by the thousands then became the streaming currents of rivers of blood.

sanskrit: prahatanararathāśvakuñjaraṃ; pratibhayadarśanam ulbaṇaṃ tadā tad ahitanihataṃ babhau balaṃ; pitṛpatirāṣṭram iva prajākṣaye
english: With its men, chariots, horses, and elephants struck down, dreadful to behold and terrible, that host, slain by the foe, looked then like the realm of the Lord of the ancestors at the destruction of all creatures.

sanskrit: atha tava naradeva sainikās; tava ca sutāḥ surasūnusaṃnibhāḥ amitabalapuraḥsarā raṇe; kuruvṛṣabhāḥ śiniputram abhyayuḥ
english: Then your soldiers, O lord of men, and your sons, like the sons of the gods, with hosts of measureless might before them, those bulls of the Kurus, advanced in battle against the son of Śini.

sanskrit: tad atirucirabhīmam ābabhau; puruṣavarāśvarathadvipākulam lavaṇajalasamuddhatasvanaṃ; balam amarāsurasainyasaṃnibham
english: Most splendid and terrible it appeared, that host thronged with the best of men, with horses, chariots, and elephants, roaring like the upheaved waters of the salt sea, resembling the armies of gods and demons.

sanskrit: surapatisamavikramas tatas; tridaśavarāvarajopamaṃ yudhi dinakarakiraṇaprabhaiḥ pṛṣatkai; ravitanayo 'bhyahanac chinipravīram
english: Then the son of the Sun, in valor the equal of the lord of the gods, struck in the fight the hero of the Śinis—who was like the younger brother of the chief of the immortals—with shafts bright as the rays of the day-maker.

sanskrit: tam api sarathavājisārathiṃ; śinivṛṣabho vividhaiḥ śarais tvaran bhujagaviṣasamaprabhai raṇe; puruṣavaraṃ samavāstṛṇot tadā
english: Him too—that best of men, together with his chariot, horses, and charioteer—the bull of the Śinis, hastening, then covered over in the fight with arrows of various kinds, gleaming like the venom of serpents.

sanskrit: śinivṛṣabhaśaraprapīḍitaṃ; tava suhṛdo vasuṣeṇam abhyayuḥ tvaritam atirathā ratharṣabhaṃ; dviradarathāśvapadātibhiḥ saha
english: Vasuṣeṇa, hard pressed by the arrows of the bull of the Śinis—to him, that bull among car-warriors, your friends, mighty car-warriors, swiftly hastened with elephants, chariots, horses, and foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: tam udadhinibham ādravad balī; tvaritataraiḥ samabhidrutaṃ paraiḥ drupadasutasakhas tadākarot; puruṣarathāśvagajakṣayaṃ mahat
english: Upon that host, vast as the ocean, assailed by the foes that rushed on still more swiftly, the mighty comrade of Drupada's son charged, and wrought then a great destruction of men, chariots, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: atha puruṣavarau kṛtāhnikau; bhavam abhipūjya yathāvidhi prabhum arivadhakṛtaniścayau drutaṃ; tava balam arjunakeśavau sṛtau
english: Then those two best of men, their daily rites performed, having duly worshipped Lord Bhava, resolved upon the slaying of the foe, Arjuna and Keśava swiftly bore down upon your host.

sanskrit: jaladaninadanisvanaṃ rathaṃ; pavanavidhūtapatākaketanam sitahayam upayāntam antikaṃ; hṛtamanaso dadṛśus tadārayaḥ
english: That chariot, rumbling like a rain-cloud, its banner and standard shaken by the wind, drawn by white horses, approaching near—the foes beheld it then, their senses stolen away.

sanskrit: atha visphārya gāṇḍīvaṃ raṇe nṛtyann ivārjunaḥ śarasaṃbādham akarot khaṃ diśaḥ pradiśas tathā
english: Then twanging the Gāṇḍīva, dancing as it were upon the field, Arjuna filled the sky, the quarters, and the intermediate quarters with a dense press of arrows.

sanskrit: rathān vimānapratimān sajjayantrāyudhadhvajān sasārathīṃs tadā bāṇair abhrāṇīvānilo 'vadhīt
english: Chariots like celestial cars, equipped with their gear, weapons, and banners, together with their charioteers, he then struck down with his arrows as the wind scatters the clouds.

sanskrit: gajān gajaprayantṝṃś ca vaijayantyāyudhadhvajān sādino 'śvāṃś ca pattīṃś ca śarair ninye yamakṣayam
english: Elephants and their drivers, with their pennons, weapons, and banners, and horsemen and horses and foot-soldiers, he sent with his arrows to the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: tam antakam iva kruddham anivāryaṃ mahāratham duryodhano 'bhyayād eko nighnan bāṇaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ
english: Against him, like enraged Death himself, irresistible, that great car-warrior, Duryodhana advanced alone, smiting with arrows of various kinds.

sanskrit: tasyārjuno dhanuḥ sūtaṃ ketum aśvāṃś ca sāyakaiḥ hatvā saptabhir ekaikaṃ chatraṃ ciccheda patriṇā
english: Arjuna, slaying his bow, his charioteer, his standard, and his horses—each with seven shafts—cut through his parasol with a feathered arrow.

sanskrit: navamaṃ ca samāsādya vyasṛjat pratighātinam duryodhanāyeṣuvaraṃ taṃ drauṇiḥ saptadhācchinat
english: And taking up a ninth, a piercing one, he loosed that excellent shaft at Duryodhana; but the son of Droṇa cut it into seven pieces.

sanskrit: tato drauṇer dhanuś chittvā hatvā cāśvavarāñ śaraiḥ kṛpasyāpi tathātyugraṃ dhanuś ciccheda pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then, cutting the bow of Droṇa's son and slaying his fine horses with arrows, the Pāṇḍava likewise severed the most terrible bow of Kṛpa as well.

sanskrit: hārdikyasya dhanuś chittvā dhvajaṃ cāśvaṃ tathāvadhīt duḥśāsanasyeṣuvaraṃ chittvā rādheyam abhyayāt
english: Cutting the bow of Hārdikya, he slew likewise his banner and his horse; and severing the excellent shaft of Duḥśāsana, he advanced upon Rādheya.

sanskrit: atha sātyakim utsṛjya tvaran karṇo 'rjunaṃ tribhiḥ viddhvā vivyādha viṃśatyā kṛṣṇaṃ pārthaṃ punas tribhiḥ
english: Then, leaving off Sātyaki, Karṇa, hastening, pierced Arjuna with three arrows, struck Kṛṣṇa with twenty, and the son of Pṛthā again with three.

sanskrit: atha sātyakir āgatya karṇaṃ viddhvā śitaiḥ śaraiḥ navatyā navabhiś cograiḥ śatena punar ārdayat
english: Then Sātyaki, coming up, pierced Karṇa with sharp arrows—with ninety-nine fierce ones—and tormented him again with a hundred.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravīrāḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ sarve karṇam apīḍayan yudhāmanyuḥ śikhaṇḍī ca draupadeyāḥ prabhadrakāḥ
english: Then all the foremost heroes of the Pāṇḍavas pressed Karṇa hard—Yudhāmanyu and Śikhaṇḍin and the sons of Draupadī and the Prabhadrakas.

sanskrit: uttamaujā yuyutsuś ca yamau pārṣata eva ca cedikārūṣamatsyānāṃ kekayānāṃ ca yad balam cekitānaś ca balavān dharmarājaś ca suvrataḥ
english: Uttamaujas and Yuyutsu, the twins, and the grandson of Pṛṣata, and the host of the Cedis, Karūṣas, and Matsyas, and of the Kekayas, and the mighty Cekitāna, and the Dharma-king of noble vows—

sanskrit: ete rathāśvadviradaiḥ pattibhiś cogravikramaiḥ parivārya raṇe karṇaṃ nānāśastrair avākiran bhāṣanto vāgbhir ugrābhiḥ sarve karṇavadhe vṛtāḥ
english: These, with chariots, horses, and elephants and with foot-soldiers of fierce valor, surrounded Karṇa in the battle and showered him with manifold weapons, all uttering harsh words, all bent upon the slaying of Karṇa.

sanskrit: tāṃ śastravṛṣṭiṃ bahudhā chittvā karṇaḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ apovāha sma tān sarvān drumān bhaṅktveva mārutaḥ
english: That rain of weapons Karṇa cut apart in many ways with his sharp arrows, and swept them all away, as the wind sweeps away trees after breaking them.

sanskrit: rathinaḥ samahāmātrān gajān aśvān sasādinaḥ śaravrātāṃś ca saṃkruddho nighnan karṇo vyadṛśyata
english: Car-warriors, elephants with their mahouts, and horses with their riders, and the swarms of arrows—all these Karṇa, enraged, was seen smiting down.

sanskrit: tad vadhyamānaṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ balaṃ karṇāstratejasā viśastrakṣatadehaṃ ca prāya āsīt parāṅmukham
english: That host of the Pāṇḍavas, being slain by the blazing might of Karṇa's weapons, its bodies stripped of arms and wounded, well-nigh turned its face away in flight.
